hookArchitectureFacts.stopHookBehavior: Stop hooks fire after EVERY agent turn. Command-type Stop hooks output stderr which is shown to the agent as feedback on the next turn. Exit 0 = allow, Exit 2 = block. Must be fast (<50ms per surfacing-duty-stop.sh header comment).
hookArchitectureFacts.existingStopHook: surfacing-duty-stop.sh (5.1KB) — Two functions: (1) periodic surfacing duty reminder every 30 min, (2) incident-acknowledgment detection. Reads JSON from stdin (session_id, transcript_path). Uses temp marker files at /tmp/aitools-surfacing-$session_id/. Performance: reads last 100 lines of transcript, runs grep. Should be well under 50ms.
hookArchitectureFacts.hookInputContract: Stop hook receives JSON on stdin with session_id, transcript_path. Per CC tool-ops reference item #2: SessionEnd hook gets session_id, cwd, transcript_path. Per item #21 (CC 2.1.68+): agent_id and agent_type also available in hook events.
hookArchitectureFacts.hookTypes: command (runs shell, stderr = agent feedback), prompt (static string injected), http (POST to URL). For dynamic dashboard updates, command type is required (needs to write files).
hookArchitectureFacts.instructionsLoadedEvent: CC 2.1.68+ has InstructionsLoaded hook event (item #20). Fires after CLAUDE.md and rules load. Could seed initial dashboard state.
hookArchitectureFacts.sessionStartHook: scratch-init.sh already exists. channel-init.sh is PROPOSED but not built. Dashboard state could be seeded at SessionStart.

options.name: Stop hook writes full HTML each turn
options.cons: REJECTED — too slow. Full HTML generation (700+ lines of template) cannot complete in <50ms. Would block every agent turn.

options.name: Stop hook writes JSON data file, HTML reads via fetch/setInterval
options.pros: Hook writes ~2KB JSON (fast, <10ms). HTML uses setInterval to re-read the JSON and re-render client-side. Separation of data (JSON) and presentation (HTML). JSON can be consumed by other tools.
options.cons: HTML must be opened in a browser. fetch() from file:// requires the JSON to be at a known relative path. Requires generating the HTML template once at session start.
options.verdict: RECOMMENDED — best balance of speed, simplicity, and extensibility

implementation.hookAction: Stop hook appends/overwrites .aitools/channel/session-*/dashboard-state.json after each turn. The JSON contains the current session state: agents launched, their status, session metrics, decisions, assumptions, active threads.
implementation.htmlTemplate: A static HTML template with setInterval(fetch('./dashboard-state.json'), 3000) — polls every 3 seconds. The template is generated once at session start (or first delegation).
implementation.dataFlow: Agent turn completes -> Stop hook fires -> hook reads transcript tail + scratch dir -> writes dashboard-state.json -> Browser polls -> client-side JS renders

options.name: Stop hook appends to JSONL log, dashboard reads log
options.pros: Append-only (no data loss), natural time series
options.cons: JSONL grows unbounded. Dashboard must parse entire log on each poll. More complex client-side code. No random access to current state.
options.verdict: VIABLE but inferior to B. Consider as enrichment: JSONL for history, JSON for current state.

options.name: Hybrid: B + C — JSON for current state, JSONL for event log
options.pros: Best of both: fast current-state polling + full event history for time-series. Dashboard can show both live state and timeline.
options.cons: Two files to maintain in the hook. Slightly more complexity.
options.verdict: OPTIMAL for a full mission control dashboard. Recommend implementing B first, adding JSONL event log as enrichment.

dataGathering.fromTranscript: Agent count (grep for Agent tool_use blocks), turn count, token estimates (line count heuristic)
dataGathering.fromScratchDir: AAR files (m*.json), running estimate, proposals, dashboards, writeblocked files
dataGathering.fromMarkerFiles: Delegation log entries written by the S3 during delegation (per-agent status files)

reibung.transcript_size: Transcript can be 10MB+. The hook MUST NOT read the full transcript. Use tail -N or seek to end. The existing surfacing-duty-stop.sh already uses tail -100.
reibung.scratch_dir_scan: ls of scratch dir is fast (<1ms). stat of individual files adds up. Limit to known patterns (m*.json, running-estimate*.json, s2*.json).
reibung.concurrent_hooks: Multiple Stop hooks fire sequentially. Adding a dashboard hook adds latency to EVERY turn. Must be absolutely minimal.
reibung.file_write_overhead: Writing ~2KB JSON via printf/echo is <1ms. This is negligible.
reibung.browser_polling: fetch() from file:// works in Chrome (tested with chrome-devtools MCP). Safari may require a local server. Recommend: open in Chrome.

s1PerPlanningBrief.decision24: Agents are sensors not filers. Findings flow: channel -> S2 consolidation -> S1 incident filing. S1 is delegated by S2 at plan end.
s1PerPlanningBrief.decision25: S1 (Administration) = incident filer, assigned by S2, function not rank. Any agent can hold the S1 function.
s1PerPlanningBrief.decision26: S1 waits till end. S2 spawned at plan start (intelligence prep) and plan end (consolidation). S1 spawned by S2 only at plan end.
s1PerPlanningBrief.currentStatus: S1 has NEVER been launched in any session. Zero S3->S2->S1 chains ever executed. Decision D-S1-LAUNCH (this session) defines the implementation details but S1 remains unexecuted.

s1AndDashboard.analysis: The planning brief defines S1 as an incident filer launched at plan end. But a mission control dashboard is continuous session bookkeeping — it needs maintenance throughout the session, not just at the end. Three options exist for S1's role in dashboard maintenance.

options.name: Stop hook IS the S1 function (no agent needed)
options.description: The Stop hook automatically updates dashboard-state.json after every turn. No S1 agent is launched. The hook performs mechanical bookkeeping (counting agents, tracking status, computing metrics). This is administration-as-code, not administration-as-agent.
options.pros: Zero context cost. Completely deterministic. No subagent overhead. Fires on every turn automatically. Cannot be forgotten or skipped.
options.cons: Limited to data the hook can extract mechanically from the transcript and scratch files. Cannot do qualitative analysis (e.g., 'this agent deviated from its mission').
options.verdict: RECOMMENDED for the first implementation. The mechanical dashboard data (agent count, status, metrics, timeline) is exactly what a hook can extract. Quality analysis is S2's job, not S1's.

options.name: S1 subagent launched periodically for enrichment
options.description: The hook handles mechanical updates. At key moments (after every 5th delegation, at session midpoint, before handoff), the S3 launches an S1 subagent that reads the dashboard-state.json, enriches it with qualitative analysis (convergence patterns, deviation trends, assumption status), and writes an enriched version.
options.pros: Adds intelligence to the dashboard (not just data). S1 can spot patterns the hook cannot.
options.cons: Consumes context tokens. Requires delegation duty. S1 agent must read dashboard-state.json + scratch files. Adds latency at enrichment points.
options.verdict: VIABLE as Phase 2 enhancement. Not needed for MVP.

options.name: Hybrid: hook for mechanical, S1 for enrichment at handoff
options.description: Stop hook maintains dashboard-state.json throughout the session (Option A). At session end, before /handoff, S2 launches S1 to produce a FINAL dashboard enrichment: add convergence analysis, assumption verification status, proposal ranking, session narrative. This enriched dashboard becomes part of the handoff artifact.
options.pros: Gets the best of both: continuous mechanical updates + one-time enrichment at session end. Aligns with decision #26 (S1 waits till end).
options.cons: S1 still only fires once. Dashboard enrichment is valuable throughout, not just at end.
options.verdict: RECOMMENDED as the target architecture. MVP is Option A (hook only). Option C adds S1 enrichment at session end.

s1AndDashboard.recommendation: Phase 1: Option A (hook only). Phase 2: Option C (hook + S1 enrichment at session end). This respects decision #26 (S1 waits till end) while delivering continuous dashboard updates via the hook.

section5_dashboardDataModel.rationale: The dashboard-state.json is the bridge between the Stop hook (writer) and the HTML dashboard (reader). It must be fast to write (hook budget: <15ms), fast to read (browser poll: <100ms parse), and contain enough data for all dashboard sections.

meta.schwerpunkt: string — from running estimate or delegation prompt
meta.contextEstimate: string — e.g., '~45% used' (heuristic from transcript size)

agents.aarFile: string|null — path to AAR JSON if produced

section5_dashboardDataModel.sizeEstimate: With 20 agents, 8 decisions, 22 assumptions, 7 open threads, 30 recent activities: ~8-12KB JSON. Comfortably within the <15ms write budget and <100ms parse budget.

agentData.primary: Read running-estimate-v4.json delegationLog array. Each entry has: id, type, mission, agentType, status, dutyFulfilled, deviation. This is the AUTHORITATIVE source for agent data — the S3 maintains it.
agentData.fallback: If no running estimate exists (ad-hoc session), scan scratch dir for m*-aar.json files and extract mission/status from their meta sections.
agentData.limitation: The hook cannot know about agents launched AFTER the running estimate was last updated. The running estimate may be stale by 1-2 turns. This is acceptable — the dashboard shows the last-known state.

governanceData.primary: Read running-estimate-v4.json decisions, assumptions, findings, openThreads arrays.
governanceData.limitation: Same staleness issue. The S3 must update the running estimate frequently for the dashboard to be accurate.

metricsData.sessionDuration: stat birth time of transcript vs current time
metricsData.tokenEstimate: Heuristic: transcript_bytes / 4 (rough tokens-per-byte for mixed JSON/text)

caveats.title: .gitignore blocker — dashboard files will be gitignored
caveats.description: .gitignore line 47 blanket-ignores .aitools/. The dashboard HTML and JSON would be at .aitools/channel/session-*/mission-control.html and .aitools/channel/session-*/dashboard-state.json. These are session-scoped and SHOULD be gitignored (they are ephemeral per-session files). So the .gitignore blanket is actually CORRECT for these files. The issue only affects CARRY-FORWARD files (running-estimate.json).
caveats.impact: LOW for the dashboard itself. The dashboard files are session-ephemeral. They do not need to survive across sessions.
caveats.mitigation: None needed for dashboard files. The .gitignore fix remains critical for running estimate carry-forward but does not block the dashboard.

caveats.title: Running estimate maintenance dependency
caveats.description: The dashboard reads its agent data from the running estimate's delegationLog. If the S3 does not maintain the running estimate, the dashboard shows stale data. In this session (5HyCwPtSDH), the running estimate was maintained but had a version collision (two v4 files). In future sessions, there is no enforcement that the running estimate is updated after each delegation.
caveats.impact: Dashboard accuracy depends on S3 discipline. Missing agents, wrong status, stale counts.
caveats.mitigation: Phase 1: accept staleness. Phase 2: hook writes per-delegation marker files (one JSON per launched agent) that the dashboard hook reads. This removes the dependency on running estimate freshness for agent tracking. The running estimate remains the source for governance data (decisions, assumptions).

caveats.title: Stop hook performance chain
caveats.description: Multiple Stop hooks fire sequentially. Currently: surfacing-duty-stop.sh. Adding dashboard-state-stop.sh adds a second hook. Both must complete before the agent's next turn begins. Combined budget: <30ms (15ms each).
caveats.impact: If the dashboard hook is slow (e.g., reading large running estimate), it delays every agent turn.
caveats.mitigation: Dashboard hook reads only: (1) a marker dir for agent count (ls, <1ms), (2) the running estimate meta section (head -5, <1ms), (3) transcript line count (wc -l, <1ms). Total: <5ms. Well within budget.

caveats.title: HTML template generation — when and by whom
caveats.description: The static HTML template (with CSS and JS for polling/rendering) must be generated once per session. Options: (a) generated by scratch-init.sh at SessionStart, (b) generated by the S3 at first delegation, (c) generated by the dashboard-state hook on first invocation.
caveats.impact: If generated at SessionStart, every session gets a dashboard even if no agents are launched. If generated at first delegation, no dashboard until the S3 delegates.
caveats.mitigation: Generate on first hook invocation that detects agent data exists. Lazy generation avoids unnecessary files in sessions without delegations.

caveats.title: Channel infrastructure is NOT BUILT
caveats.description: Per M18 finding: channels (decisions #22-24) were never built. No /channel skill, no schemas, no session dirs. The dashboard would write to .aitools/channel/session-*/dashboard-state.json but .aitools/channel/ does not exist in practice.
caveats.impact: The dashboard hook must create the directory structure itself (mkdir -p).
caveats.mitigation: The hook creates .aitools/channel/session-$session_id/ via mkdir -p if it does not exist. This is the same pattern scratch-init.sh uses. The full channel infrastructure can be built later; the dashboard only needs the directory to exist.

observations.fact: All 4 dashboards in this session were generated by Python scripts or inline agent writes. None used a reusable template or hook-based generation. Each dashboard was a one-off craft.
observations.implication: Dashboard generation is currently artisanal, not industrialized. The mission control dashboard introduces the first reusable, auto-updating dashboard infrastructure.

observations.fact: The governance dashboard (decisions/assumptions/proposals) uses HARDCODED HTML with no JS data layer. Every card is hand-written HTML. This cannot be dynamically updated.
observations.implication: The unified dashboard must use a JS data model (like the v2 activity dashboard's const agents=[...]) for ALL sections, including governance. The governance data must come from the JSON state file, not from hardcoded HTML.

observations.fact: The running estimate already contains ALL the data needed for the dashboard: delegationLog (agents), decisions, assumptions, findings, openThreads, completedWork, deviations, facts. The dashboard is a VIEW of the running estimate.
observations.implication: The dashboard hook's primary job is reading the running estimate and formatting it as dashboard-state.json. The HTML template's job is rendering that JSON. This is a classic model-view separation.

observations.fact: The D-DASHBOARD-GOVERNANCE decision (this session) says 'Dashboard production is S2 duty in Operational Learning framework' with standard naming and tracked location. But decision #36 component 8 says channel-archive.sh archives severity >= high to .aitools/harvesting/. A session-end dashboard snapshot should be archived.
observations.implication: The mission control dashboard should have a 'snapshot' mode: at session end, the current dashboard-state.json is frozen and the HTML+JSON pair is copied to harvesting/ as a permanent record. This connects dashboard production to the operational learning pipeline.

discrepancies.finding: running-estimate-v4.json completedWork[45] claims '.gitignore fix applied' but .gitignore:47 still has blanket '.aitools/'. VERIFIED FALSE on re-read. This is the same false claim M19 identified. The SHIP agent must be warned.
discrepancies.severity: HIGH — if the SHIP agent trusts the running estimate, it may assume .aitools/ paths work when they are gitignored

discrepancies.finding: D-DASHBOARD-GOVERNANCE says dashboard is an S2 duty, but this brief recommends dashboard maintenance via a Stop hook (mechanical S1 function). The decision and implementation diverge on WHO maintains the dashboard.
discrepancies.severity: LOW — the decision governs the PRODUCTION of dashboards (S2 consolidation duty at session end). The Stop hook handles MECHANICAL updates during the session. These are complementary, not contradictory. S2 produces the final enriched dashboard; the hook maintains the live state.

proposals.proposal: After building the dashboard, propose amending D-DASHBOARD-GOVERNANCE to distinguish mechanical dashboard maintenance (hook/S1 function) from analytical dashboard production (S2 duty). The current decision only covers S2.
The dashboard-state.json schema should be versioned (schemaVersion field) so the HTML template can handle backward-compatible changes without breaking.
